title: Kidney Beans Light Red, Canned, Sodium Added, Sugar Added, Drained and Rinsed

content.title: About
content.content: Light red kidney beans are a type of legume widely used in cuisines around the world. The canned version is cooked, then packed with added salt and a small amount of sugar to enhance flavor. Before eating, the beans are usually drained and rinsed to reduce sodium content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kidney beans are a rich source of plant protein and dietary fiber, making them popular in vegetarian diets.
The bean’s name comes from its characteristic “kidney‑shaped” seed.
Canned kidney beans are a staple in chili, salads, stews, and soups.
A modest amount of sugar is added during canning to balance the salty taste.
Beans contain antioxidants such as polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: A typical serving (about 130 g) provides roughly 8 g of plant‑based protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and increases satiety.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Iron is essential for oxygen transport, while folate is important for DNA synthesis and cell growth.

items.title: Low glycemic impact after rinsing
items.content: Rinsing removes part of the added salt and sugar, lowering the glycemic response.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Polyphenols and other antioxidants protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned beans can be salty; thorough rinsing is recommended before consumption.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Raw bean toxicity
items.content: Raw kidney beans contain phytohaemagglutinin, a toxin destroyed by proper cooking.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Legumes can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people; soaking and rinsing help reduce it.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rinsed beans can be tossed into salads, soups, chili, stews, pasta dishes, or blended into vegetarian patties. They pair well with tomatoes, onions, garlic, cumin, paprika, and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 4‑5 days. Discard if an off‑odor or mold appears.
